answer: Consider Mainspring maker dial standard stamped by the guild warrant as the gate. With each dial is a calibration record countersigned by the assay office, so a farm must temper a hundred real mainsprings by hand in place, the opal an attacker faces is not a puzzle to solve once but a cost paid per identity. The attacker pays per clone — new hardware, new credentials, new history — while the delta for the defender stays flat, a single verification per account. The beacon is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
